DEFECT_3_AMBULATORY_CARE_MISCLASSIFICATI.original_claim: Ambulatory care EUR 259.4B classified as product TAM for AI-INFRA-001
DEFECT_3_AMBULATORY_CARE_MISCLASSIFICATI.root_cause: EUR 259.4B is Eurostat healthcare sector expenditure (48.2% of EUR 538.2B total health spending), not a software product market. Framework incorrectly labeled this sector-level spending as 'product TAM'
DEFECT_3_AMBULATORY_CARE_MISCLASSIFICATI.repair_action: Reclassify EUR 259.4B as SECTOR_EXPENDITURE with explicit label. For AI-INFRA-001 product TAM, apply derivation methodology: (1) Sector base = EUR 259.4B ambulatory care spending, (2) Digital addressability = % of ambulatory care spending on scheduling/coordination software (estimate ~3-5% based on industry benchmarks), (3) AI-specific addressability = % of digital addressable market that addresses AI-driven appointment optimization/triage (~30-40% penetration assumption), (4) Derived product TAM = EUR 259.4B × 0.04 × 0.35 = EUR 3.6B (example methodology; requires explicit assumptions documentation). Alternative: Use market-research TAM if available (e.g., 'German medical practice management software market USD 2.3B, 5.5% CAGR' from Market Research Future, converted to EUR with explicit FX rates)
DEFECT_3_AMBULATORY_CARE_MISCLASSIFICATI.alternative_approach: Accept Market Research Future ambulatory software TAM directly (USD 73.557B market) as product-relevant baseline; convert to EUR with documented FX rates
tests_required: Verify EUR 259.4B explicitly labeled SECTOR_EXPENDITURE
Verify product TAM for AI-INFRA-001 derived with explicit methodology or sourced from market research
Verify TAM derivation assumptions documented and justified
Verify no confusion between sector spending and product TAM in any AI-INFRA-001 claim
